data.name: Curaçao
data.summary: Curaçao taxes residents on worldwide income; portfolio capital gains are exempt but dividends are taxed at progressive rates up to 46.5% (19.5% from a 5%+ stake). Inheritance and gift tax applies to Curaçao-domiciled persons, with children paying 2%-6% above an XCG 80,000 exemption. The penshonado regime (age 50+, home of NAf 450,000+) taxes foreign income at 10%. No wealth tax. The currency is the Caribbean guilder (XCG), which replaced the NAf/ANG in 2025.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Residents are taxed on worldwide income under a schedular system with progressive rates up to 46.5%. Passive capital gains are exempt except on a substantial shareholding (5%+), taxed at 19.5%. Inheritance and gift tax applies when the deceased/donor is a Curaçao resident.
regimes.eligibility: Residence based on facts and circumstances (centre of existence in Curaçao). Dutch nationals have a right of admission (with conditions); others need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains of private (non-business) investors are exempt, except gains on a substantial shareholding (5% or more), which are taxed at a special 19.5% rate. Business gains are taxed at progressive rates.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: On emigration with a 5%+ stake, a protective assessment on the built-in gain may be imposed, collected on later dividends or sale. Real estate transfer tax 4% (buyer).

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Curaçao Highlights 2026

open_questions: Primary legislation for the 19.5% rate and the 5% threshold not opened.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Deloitte Curaçao Highlights 2026: passive gains exempt unless substantial interest (5%+); special 19.5% rate applies to income from a substantial share interest. private_business_sale assumes a 5%+ stake. Real estate gains of a private investor treated as exempt (not business).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Gains forming part of an entrepreneur's profits are taxed at the progressive rates (up to 46.5%).

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxable income from movable assets at progressive rates up to 46.5% (top bracket above XCG 162,894 in 2026); dividends from a substantial interest at 19.5%. No relief for foreign tax in the law, though a deduction from gross foreign income may be allowed.

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Curaçao Highlights 2026

open_questions: Whether all portfolio dividends (domestic and foreign) are taxed at the full progressive rates was inferred from Deloitte's schedular description; not confirmed in the ordinance.
dividends.rate_basis: Deloitte 2026 top marginal rate 46.5% applied to portfolio dividends (income from movable assets). Curaçao levies no dividend withholding tax.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends, interest or royalties (8.5% only on resident individuals' interest from domestic banks).
dividends.treaty_network: Four tax treaties plus the Tax Arrangement for the Kingdom of the Netherlands; no treaty with the US that reduces US withholding on dividends for residents (not verified in detail).

sources.title: Deloitte International Tax: Curaçao Highlights 2026

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Real estate tax 0.4% up to XCG 350,000, 0.5% to XCG 750,000, 0.6% above. Transfer tax 4% on acquisition of real estate.

inheritance.summary: Successiebelasting is levied on inheritances from, and gifts by, a Curaçao resident (woonplaats). Children: XCG 80,000 exemption per child on inheritance (XCG 20,000 per year on gifts), then 2% up to XCG 50,000, 4% to XCG 250,000 and 6% above. Non-resident deceased: only an 8% transfer tax (overgangsbelasting) on Curaçao real estate.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Acquisitions by a private foundation (SPF) or trust are taxed at a flat 25% (art. 61(2)-(3)); distributions from an SPF or trust to beneficiaries are exempt (art. 56(1) 8° and 9°). Pension and annuity rights to spouse/children exempt.

open_questions: Art. 61 says the tax is levied 'progressively' using the table; whether each rate applies only to the slice (marginal, assumed) or to the whole amount is not explicit.
An opposition party called for abolition in Sept 2026; no bill found.
inheritance.spouse_note: The surviving spouse (or life partner) has a deduction of XCG 240,000 against XCG 80,000 for a child, and pays the same 2%/4%/6% scale as children (Successiebelastingverordening 1908 arts. 1A, 60 and 61).
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts by a Curaçao resident are taxed with the same table; annual exemption XCG 20,000 for gifts from parents to children (art. 60(b)); personal-use movables up to XCG 10,000 exempt.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Worldwide estate of a resident deceased is taxed; the 2022 unilateral decree for avoidance of double taxation may give relief (not verified).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Tax applies if the deceased or donor had his woonplaats (domicile) in Curaçao (art. 1, 4). No trailing period after emigration found (art. 4(2) repealed).

regimes.name: Penshonado regime (arts. 23B-23E Income Tax Ordinance)
regimes.description: New residents aged 50+ may elect a 10% flat rate on foreign-source income (art. 23B), or treat foreign income as a deemed amount of NAf/XCG 500,000 taxed at progressive rates (art. 23C).
regimes.eligibility: At least 60 consecutive months living outside Curaçao before the year of first application; aged 50+ at registration; notify the Inspector within 2 months of registration; within 18 months use an owned, unrented home in Curaçao (or a protected monument) worth at least NAf 450,000; admitted under immigration law; no Curaçao business or employment income (with exceptions).
regimes.duration_note: No time limit: arts. 23B-23E of the Income Tax Ordinance 1943 set no end date or maximum period. The regime applies for every year in which the conditions of art. 23D continue to be met (own, unrented home in Curaçao for own use worth at least NAf 450,000); it lapses for any year in which the taxpayer or a non-separated spouse earns business or employment income in Curaçao (art. 23D(3)).

capital_gains.summary: Foreign substantial-interest share gains are foreign-source income taxed at 10%; portfolio gains remain exempt.

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends and foreign interest taxed at 10% flat. Alternatively, total foreign income can be deemed to be NAf 500,000 and taxed progressively (worth it only for very large foreign income).

data.us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain subject to US federal income, estate and gift tax on worldwide income and assets; the app adds the federal layer. Local tax can generally be credited against US tax on the same foreign-source income only where the US foreign tax credit rules allow. No US-Curaçao income tax treaty was confirmed.

Portfolio dividend taxation for ordinary residents inferred from Deloitte, not from the ordinance.

succession.name: Curaçao
succession.summary: Curaçao has no forced heirship, so a will can leave the estate to anyone, though children and a spouse have statutory lump-sum rights. Curaçao has its own trust (since 2012) and a private foundation (stichting particulier fonds). The Hague Trusts Convention has been in force for Curaçao since 1 February 2024.
succession.family_claims: The Caribbean Book 4 replaced the legitieme portie with mandatory statutory rights (a child's lump sum for upbringing and unpaid work, arts. 4:35-36 in the Sint Maarten text, and spousal rights). Curaçao's own text was not read.
succession.foreign_law_note: No source read states Curaçao's conflict rule for a foreign national's estate. A 2023 article says a conflict-of-laws ordinance for trusts was still intended.
succession.trust_note: The HCCH extensions page lists Curaçao (extension 27 November 2023, in force 1 February 2024). Curaçao has a trust created by notarial deed since 1 January 2012 (secondary source). The stichting particulier fonds is a private foundation that may distribute to the founder's family and cannot run a business.
open_questions: Date Curaçao's Book 4 entered into force was not confirmed; a 2021 Dutch parliamentary question says Curaçao has no legitieme portie.
Statute articles for the Curaçao trust were not read (source is a paywalled summary).
Conflict rule for succession of foreign nationals not sourced.
